name: Olaf Tryggvason and Norway's Christianization
summary: Olaf Tryggvason seizes the Norwegian throne and undertakes a violent Christianization campaign, destroying pagan temples, executing holdout pagans, and sending missionaries to Iceland, Greenland, the Faroe Islands, and Orkney. His reign (995-1000) initiates the Christianization of Scandinavia. Though Olaf dies at the Battle of Svolder (1000), his successor Olaf Haraldsson (Saint Olaf) completes the process.

_quarry.structural_significance: Norwegian Christianization ends the institutional Norse paganism that had sustained Viking Age culture; Christian conversion brings literacy (from the church), Roman legal concepts, and integration into the European diplomatic network; it also subordinates the Norse kingdoms to Rome's ecclesiastical authority, ending the ideological distinctiveness that had made the Vikings a uniquely disruptive external force
